metadata.neutral_citation: YIM FAT FONG v. WONG KIM HUNG AND ANOTHER [1999] HKCFI 1055; HCPI 1173/1996 (24 June 1999)
metadata.case_name: YIM FAT FONG v. WONG KIM HUNG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: self-employed poultry dealer supplying chickens, ducks and geese to, for the most part, restaurants and, to a lesser extent, cooked meat stalls

injuries.description: There was a head injury with no apparent brain damage or lesion - a scalp laceration needed suturing and he was recorded as having been unconscious for in excess of two hours in one report, though in fact the period may well have been as little as half-an-hour or less.
source: There was a head injury with no apparent brain damage or lesion - a scalp laceration needed suturing and he was recorded as having been unconscious for in excess of two hours in one report, though in fact the period may well have been as little as half-an-hour or less.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture dislocation of the 6th and 7th cervical vertebrae which was treated with open reduction and metal wire fixation approximately one week after admission to hospital. This was a spinal fusion at this level.
source: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture dislocation of the 6th and 7th cervical vertebrae which was treated with open reduction and metal wire fixation approximately one week after admission to hospital. This was a spinal fusion at this level.

injuries.description: there were other more minor injuries to the left shoulder, and left eyebrow.
source: there were other more minor injuries to the left shoulder, and left eyebrow.
injuries.icd_description: Superficial injury of shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

manifestations.description: numbness over his fingers, especially those of his right hand; numbness in the right thumb, index and middle fingers; residual numbness over the finger tips and weakness in the left hand and arm
clumsy gait; being prone to fall; impaired balance; unsteadiness of all four limbs; lower limb sluggish reflexes with left leg more clumsy and weaker than the right
loss of consciousness (recorded as in excess of two hours in one report, though may have been as little as half-an-hour or less)

treatments_received: open reduction and metal wire fixation (spinal fusion at C6-C7) carried out on 30th March
bone grafts taken from his iliac crest
halo-body jacket to immobilise his neck
anti-epileptic medication including Luminal, Phenytoin (Dilantin), Mysolin, Epilim, Tegretol
treatments_future: psychiatric treatment: one session a month for one year

losses.description: Could not manage those aspects of his business which involved riding a bicycle and frequent lifting of heavy weights; business effectively ended and could not be resurrected.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to ride his bicycle as required for his business and deliveries.
Impaired balance, clumsy gait, unsteadiness of limbs and a degree of disability in the legs.
Mental slowness and poor memory attributed to post-concussional disorder / head injury.
Substantial loss of amenity and quality of life following the accident.
